description.purpose: Verify the caller, find the 243.18 dollar marketplace charge, walk him through the published unauthorized-transaction procedure, and open a secure dispute session he controls, which he then leaves unsubmitted once the charge turns out to be his daughter's purchase on his saved card.
description.notes: An unfamiliar descriptor is not proof of fraud, and the right outcome is no dispute at all. The agent must not erase the charge, promise provisional credit, submit anything, or treat an issued session as a filed claim.

user_scenario.persona: A calm, practical father who is worried but cooperative. He speaks plainly, steps away to check with his daughter mid-call, and is a little embarrassed when the charge turns out to be hers.

instructions.reason_for_call: There is a 243 dollar and 18 cent charge on your credit card from a company you have never heard of. You have not filed anything yet and want to know whether you need to dispute it.
instructions.known_info:
You are Justin Porter.
The email on your profile is jporter92@email.com.
Your billing ZIP code is 64114.
Your birthday is February 19.
The charge is 243.18 dollars. It posted on Monday, no city is listed, and the statement description reads MRKTPLC*8472 (spell it M-R-K-T-P-L-C star 8472).
Your physical card is in your wallet.
Your daughter uses that online marketplace.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know what the merchant is or who made the purchase. You do not know the bank's dispute procedure.
instructions.task_instructions:
Open by saying there is a 243 dollar and 18 cent charge from a company you have never heard of, that you have not filed anything, and that you are trying to figure out whether you need to dispute it. Give your name and email together when asked, then your ZIP and birthday when asked. When asked what you recognize, say you recognize the amount because it is on your statement, it posted Monday, there is no city, and the description says M-R-K-T-P-L-C star 8472.

Say you did not buy anything for 243 dollars online. Confirm your card is in your wallet. When asked about household use, say your daughter has used the marketplace but not your card, and that you will ask her now. At some point ask whether the agent can just remove the charge. If offered the secure dispute form, say yes, you would rather have it ready while you check with your daughter. Once it is ready, say you can see it and that it asks whether you contacted the merchant; then that it asks whether you want a representative. Say you can finish it yourself and ask what happens after you submit. Say you will call your daughter first and finish it if needed.

Then say your daughter is calling you back and ask the agent to hold. Come back and say she bought a patio set but swears she used her own card. If the agent suggests checking the card ending or a saved wallet, say you texted her, she is checking, and that this is embarrassing. Then say she found it: the receipt shows your last four digits and she clicked too fast at checkout. Do not submit the dispute. Ask whether the agent can cancel the dispute tool, then ask whether leaving it will hurt you later. Say you appreciate being made to check before filing. Ask whether you should remove your card from her account. Ask whether the final outcome is no bank dispute. Then say you are glad you figured it out, that is all, thank the agent and end the call.

nl_assertions: Agent verifies the caller's billing ZIP and birth month and day before discussing the transaction.
Agent tells the caller that it cannot erase a posted charge.
Agent tells the caller that filing a dispute does not guarantee provisional credit.
Agent tells the caller that he reviews and submits the dispute himself and that no claim is recorded until he presses Submit.
Agent tells the caller not to submit an unauthorized-transaction claim once the charge is identified as his daughter's purchase.
Agent tells the caller that leaving the dispute session unsubmitted does not waive his future dispute rights.

arguments.query: unauthorized transaction procedure for unfamiliar marketplace descriptor and possible household use

output.title: Unauthorized card transactions: review and dispute procedure
output.content: An unfamiliar charge is reviewed first for household use and for cards saved in digital wallets or merchant accounts. A dispute is submitted by the customer through the secure dispute session, and only for a transaction the customer did not authorize. A posted charge is not erased outside the dispute process. Provisional credit is not guaranteed, and investigation timing depends on the transaction type. After submission the customer receives a claim reference and written timing disclosures in secure messages.

arguments.query: Does an unused unsubmitted dispute session affect future dispute rights?

output.title: Dispute sessions: lifecycle and dispute rights
output.content: A dispute session is issued to the customer's secure message centre and completed by the customer in online banking. Issuing or opening a session does not create a claim; a claim exists only once the customer submits the form. A session that is closed or left unsubmitted ends without a claim and does not waive the customer's right to dispute that transaction or any other transaction later. A customer who later identifies a genuinely unauthorized transaction should contact the bank promptly.

events.speaker: Darren
events.text: Uh, no, it should not. If you later discover a genuinely unauthorized transaction, contact us immediately. Uh, today's unused session does not waive your rights at all.

events.text: Okay. I appreciate that you made me check before filing.

events.speaker: Darren
events.text: Yes, the policy is designated, or designed to separate merchant confusion, household use, and actual unauthorized activity. Each can require a different remedy.

events.text: That's a sensible security step you can take with the marketplace, but also review your own digital wallets and saved payment set- settings.
